text:
alex: quick question about client config for our private deployment — running into weird streaming behavior when I point the SDK at our VPC endpoint + company proxy. Anyone seen this?

maria: which SDK/lang and how are you setting the base URL / proxy?

alex: node SDK. I set `REDWOOD_API_BASE` to `https://redwood-internal.company` and also `HTTPS_PROXY=http://corp-proxy:3128`. init looks like:
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY,
  baseUrl: process.env.REDWOOD_API_BASE,
});
```
Streaming endpoints are arriving only after the request finishes (buffered). Non-streaming responses fine.

sam: corporate proxies often buffer until full response or connection close. streaming needs a proxy that supports TCP tunneling (CONNECT) and chunked transfer passthrough. Is your proxy doing TLS intercept?

alex: yes proxy is doing MITM TLS inspection. any SDK tweaks to unblock?

maria: 2 quick things: 1) prefer setting a proxy agent instead of env var if you need streaming. 2) ensure host header/SNI matches the backend hostname so TLS handshake doesn't break.

leo: Example (node + https-proxy-agent):
```js
const HttpsProxyAgent = require('https-proxy-agent');
const agent = new HttpsProxyAgent(process.env.HTTPS_PROXY);
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY,
  baseUrl: 'https://redwood-internal.company',
  httpAgent: agent, // ensure SDK passes agent to fetch/node https
});
```
That lets the proxy create a tunnel (CONNECT) so streaming flows.

alex: nice — the SDK exposes `httpAgent`? I thought it only accepted `baseUrl` and `apiKey`.

maria: current Node SDK accepts `fetchOptions`/`agent` in advanced config. If you don't, we can add an option. For product docs we should surface `httpAgent`/`httpsAgent` for corp proxies.

sam: also check transfer encoding. Proxies sometimes convert chunked->buffer. If you can curl against the proxy using `--raw` and `--no-buffer` you can confirm. e.g.:
```bash
curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy:3128 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  --no-buffer \
  https://redwood-internal.company/v1/stream
```
If you see the chunks arrive progressively it's ok. If curl waits until end, proxy buffering is the culprit.

alex: great repro commands, thanks. For auth: should we use `Authorization: Bearer` or `X-Api-Key` header for private endpoints?

maria: both are accepted by the private control plane, but prefer `Authorization: Bearer <token>` because it's standard and works with some proxy auth flows. SDK will set that if you pass `apiKey`.

leo: one more gotcha: self-signed certs in staging VPC. If TLS is terminated with internal CA you might need to provide `ca` or set `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` (not recommended). Better: add internal CA to Node's trusted store or pass `ca` in agent options.

alex: streaming improved when I switched to proxy agent + CONNECT. still seeing occasional connection resets during longer streams.

sam: that could be idle timeouts on the proxy or LB. Try keep-alive and lower-than-default chunk intervals from the server. Also set `Connection: keep-alive` and ensure the SDK uses an agent with `keepAlive: true`.

leo: sample agent config: 
```js
const agent = new HttpsProxyAgent({
  host: 'corp-proxy',
  port: 3128,
  keepAlive: true,
  timeout: 120000,
});
```
And ensure SDK re-uses agent instead of creating per-request sockets.

alex: will try. if this is a common pattern, we should add a short doc in devex about "Using proxies + private base URLs (streaming gotchas)" with the curl repro, node + python examples, and tips about SNI/CA.

maria: yes please. I'll open a tiny PR to dev docs after you confirm repro.

infra-bot: reminder: internal load balancer enforces a 300s idle TCP timeout in prod-vpc. Consider keepAlive and periodic pings.

alex: noted. thanks all. I'll test agent + CA trust, ping back in this thread. :thumbsup:

leo: if you want, drop a HAR or tcpdump snippet and I can take a look offline.

alex: will do if it still flakes.

maria: action item: add doc + SDK config option note (httpAgent/httpsAgent) — assigning to me.

alex: thanks — ending here.
